stories.title: Instant Reaction: Democrats Sweep to Control of Congress in Rebuke of Trump
stories.take: Democrats took both the House and Senate, winning Senate races in deep-red Kansas and South Carolina and governorships in Texas and Georgia • Affordability drove it — 62% of voters disapproved of Trump and two-thirds said his tariffs and economic agenda hurt more than helped • Ron Brownstein: Trump's 2024 gains with non-white working-class voters were erased in one night • The Republican lame-duck agenda shrinks to a defense bill, government funding, and maybe permitting reform

stories.title: Barry Diller on Big Bets, AI, and Knowing When to Walk Away
stories.take: Diller walked away from an $18B deal to take control of MGM — Vegas was his hedge against AI disintermediation, but the structure and debt killed it • His publishing bet is 'inversion': own the product (21 projects underway) instead of licensing brands for 1–2% • Google traffic is down ~60% and replaced via social and video; the business is in its 11th straight quarter of growth • On streaming: 'Netflix won — you are simply never going to beat Netflix'

stories.title: Democrats projected to take control of US Congress
stories.take: Democrats are projected to retake the House by a significant majority and win the Senate — Roy Cooper flipped North Carolina and James Talarico became Texas's first Democratic senator since 1988 • Cost of living, health care, and the Iran war drove the outperformance • A Democratic House can investigate the war and Trump's finances and block much of his agenda for his final two years

stories.title: Dems win big in midterm elections
stories.take: A blowout beyond expectations: seven Senate flips and 15+ House flips, between a 'thumping' and a 'shellacking' • A referendum on Trump — war, tariffs, $4 gas; his approval sat at 38% and 43% of voters said they voted to oppose him • Texas shock: Talarico beat Paxton 55–43 despite $412M in Republican Senate spending there • Trump is now officially a lame duck, and his kingmaker power for 2028 is in doubt

stories.title: Tom Lee: The Correction Is Over — Stocks Are About To Surge
stories.take: Lee's call: the correction is over — the Nasdaq-100 rallies at least 15% by year-end and the S&P 500 reaches 8,200–8,400 • A Democratic sweep is historically bullish: markets have rallied in the 12 months after midterms 100% of the time • AI is not a bubble yet, he argues — real revenue and productivity, unlike 1999 • Apple check: a record $115B quarter, but the $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo is cracking for some early buyers

stories.title: A Landslide Victory for Democrats
stories.take: A 'blue tsunami' — the largest congressional popular-vote win since at least 1976 (Democrats +13), with the Senate at 54 seats and a path to 56 • South Carolina flipped early; Texas delivered both a Senate seat and the governorship • The GOP trap, per Nate Cohn: you could not win a Republican primary without Trump, and you could not win a general election with him

stories.title: Will AI take my job? Ask an economist!
stories.take: The answer: not yet at scale — Stanford's Eric Brynjolfsson sees no evidence AI is causing widespread job displacement • The early hit is at entry level: 22- to 25-year-olds in AI-exposed jobs like customer service and software engineering sit almost 20% below peers • Senior workers who define projects and manage fleets of AI agents are in growing demand • MIT's Daron Acemoglu: whether new jobs of the same quality appear is 'up for grabs' — it depends on steering AI to complement humans, not replace them

stories.title: LA Mayor's race too close to call, Becerra wins CA Gov race, Prop 40 results— Morning Edition
stories.take: LA mayor's race too close to call — Nithya Raman leads Karen Bass by ~16,000 votes (about 2 points) with an estimated 63% counted • Becerra wins the governorship by 28 points, becoming California's first directly elected Latino governor • Prop 40's billionaire tax is losing by 11+ points and Prop 39's voter ID trails by 17+; Measure FD's fire-department sales tax is on pace to pass

stories.title: Democrats' Midterm Blowout, Trump Blames Candidates For Losses, Democratic Agenda
stories.take: Democrats flipped both chambers, with seven Senate flips including Texas, South Carolina, and Kansas • Mara Liasson: polls if anything understated the wave, and it had one overriding reason — Trump • Trump blames the candidates and pledges to be 'Mr. Veto,' but said he would respect the results • Hakeem Jeffries is set to become the first Black Speaker; oversight of the war, ICE, and Trump family business is coming

stories.title: A Blue Wave Just Swept Congress
stories.take: Democrats retook both chambers with seven Senate flips, on pace to hold at least 54 Senate seats • Drivers: the Iran war and affordability — nearly two-thirds of ~80,000 surveyed voters said Trump's policies made it harder to get by • Markets whipsawed on data-center fears, then recovered on relief that Trump won't contest the result; 56% of voters called data centers a major factor in their vote • CVS Health will split into two companies in early 2028

stories.title: Democrats storm to success in US midterm elections
stories.take: Democrats took both chambers in what Schumer called a generational remake of the Senate map; Trump blamed gas prices from the Iran war and leaned on his veto • The BBC's read: cost of living — groceries, tariffs, petrol — beat Trump, not ideology • Talarico's Texas win and Abdul El-Sayed becoming the first Muslim U.S. senator in Michigan headline the night • Tehran claims Trump 'lost the Senate to Iran'; in Israel, Arab-led parties hold a record 19 Knesset seats and possibly the balance of power

stories.title: Why Rian Johnson made a photo app
stories.take: The answer: Johnson hit a ceiling with the iPhone camera app and Snapseed, so he bullied his cinematographer Steve Yedlin into building Chromograph — a RAW camera app that bypasses Apple's look and applies the film look from their movies • It shoots RAW with burst merging on any iPhone, plus a grain-size slider and halation; no video, because Apple won't expose RAW video to third-party apps • Since Knives Out they shoot digital — Yedlin: 'It's easier to make digital look like film than to make film look like film' • Johnson detests HDR ('a scourge') and calls phone AI 'garbage AI nobody really wants'; he's ordered the iPhone Duo but mourns its missing telephoto
